nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). If a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-tape machine, then $p$ is computable, that is, $p$ is decidable and its Boolean characteristic function $\alpha \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is computable.
nodes.title: A predicate decided by a multi-tape machine is computable

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is co-recognizable by a multi-tape machine when its complement $\neg p$ is recognizable by a multi-tape machine.
nodes.title: Co-recognizability by multi-tape machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). Every predicate on $\alpha$ that is decidable by a multi-tape machine is decidable by a multi-stack machine.
nodes.title: Multi-tape machines decide no more than multi-stack machines

nodes.title: Decidability by multi-tape machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). Every predicate on $\alpha$ that is recognizable by a multi-tape machine is recognizable by a multi-stack machine.
nodes.title: Multi-tape machines recognize no more than multi-stack machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is recognizable by a multi-tape machine when there are a number $k$ and a deterministic Turing machine $M$ with finitely many states, a read-only input tape, $k$ work tapes and a write-only output tape, all over the Boolean alphabet, such that for every…
nodes.title: Recognizability by multi-tape machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). If a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-tape machine, then $p$ is recursively enumerable, that is, the partial function on $\alpha$ that is defined, with a trivial value, exactly where $p$ holds is partial recursive.
nodes.title: A predicate decided by a multi-tape machine is recursively enumerable

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). If a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-tape machine, then its complement $\neg p$ is recursively enumerable, that is, the partial function on $\alpha$ that is defined, with a trivial value, exactly where $\neg p$ holds is partial recursive.
nodes.title: A predicate decided by a multi-tape machine has a recursively enumerable complement

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type (it has an encoding $\mathrm{encode} : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ whose decoding is primitive recursive). If a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is recognizable by a multi-tape machine, then $p$ is recursively enumerable, that is, the partial function on $\alpha$ that is defined, with a trivial value, exactly where $p$ holds is partial recursive.
nodes.title: A predicate recognizable by a multi-tape machine is recursively enumerable

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
